page: Microsoft Azure D2d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance features a bundled 77 GB SSD. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in single-core workloads but poor results in multi-core and memory-intensive tasks. The single-core performance is highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 1618.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1889.69, both falling into the average category. However, multi-core performance is limited, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1865.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1932.07, both rated as poor. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 14.93 GB/sec for large-block read-only operations and 13.64 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the D2d_v5 is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and single-threaded applications such as text processing. It exhibits weak performance in database operations and multi-threaded tasks like software compilation. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of a local 77 GB SSD provides a dedicated storage resource, but the low resource density and weak multi-core scaling make it less suitable for demanding enterprise applications or high-throughput databases.
